divergence_justification: MIMIC-on-FHIR does not populate MedicationAdministration.identifier.value with inputevents.linkorderid; the ICU ETL neither selects nor writes that field (mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_medication_administration_icu.sql:7-23,42-100), so the declared typed NULL explains the linkorderid gap. The remaining key substitution and endtime conflict are intrinsic: lines 8-9 cast source start/end through TIMESTAMPTZ, lines 61-65 write only those transformed values to MedicationAdministration.effectivePeriod, and line 20 creates an opaque timestamp-free UUID. Source 2165-03-10 02:28 is irreversibly normalized to 03:28 in the America/New_York spring-forward gap and cannot be distinguished from a genuine 03:28 by any FHIR query. The attributed conflict is 1/8513 (0.0117%), consistent with DST-gap rarity. Representable fidelity is 8511/8513 (99.9765%), excluding linkorderid.

reopen_history.reason: Type B cast defect: TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP(REGEXP_REPLACE(col, offset-strip), "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss[.SSSSSS]") returns NULL on any shape the pinned format misses (date-only values especially), and TRY_ makes it silent -- those NULLs reach the judge as differing_null_only/gap_shaped, i.e. a parse failure disguised as a FHIR coverage gap at the lower bar. Replace every datetime mapping with a bare TRY_CAST(col AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ). See pathling-sql SKILL.md and MIMIC_NOTES.md:337.

The same ETL casts naive inputevents starttime/endtime through TIMESTAMPTZ at lines 8-9 and writes those normalized values at lines 64-65, irreversibly shifting DST-gap 02:28 values to 03:28; UUID construction at line 20 excludes timestamps, so the two key shifts and one endtime conflict cannot be recovered by any FHIR query. Representable fidelity is 8,510/8,513 (99.9648%), excluding linkorderid.
